signals.signal: Glory published Q1 results for the year ending 31/03/2027 on 07/08/2026 (first quarter Apr-Jun 2026, IFRS). EMEA overseas revenue was JPY 27,293m, +27.1% year-on-year in yen (+15.3% on a USD basis), and EMEA is now 51.1% of all Glory overseas revenue — the first quarter in which EMEA alone exceeds half. Americas was JPY 21,321m (39.9%, +2.1%) and Asia JPY 4,758m (8.9%). The whole Overseas Market segment made revenue JPY 53,373m (+16.1%) and operating profit JPY 4,666m, +104.9% — profit doubled. Group revenue was JPY 80,594m (+11.6%) and group operating profit JPY 4,847m (+49.8%). The investor deck's regional table breaks EMEA down by operating company: Glory Global Solutions (the cash-automation arm that supplies Printec's TCR line) JPY 13.3bn, up from JPY 10.0bn a year earlier; Sitrade Italia JPY 5.6bn from JPY 4.7bn; Acrelec (self-service kiosks) JPY 7.0bn from JPY 5.4bn; Flooid (retail POS software) JPY 1.2bn from JPY 1.1bn. Currency is Japanese yen throughout; the deck tabulates in hundred-million-yen units, and the sub-totals reconcile to the audited JPY 27,293m EMEA figure. Glory's stated Q1 EMEA market read is only 'demand in the retail market remains solid' — no bank-side commentary and no named CEE customer.
signals.source_name: GLORY LTD. — Supplementary Explanation of Consolidated Financial Results for the First Quarter of the Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 [IFRS], and FY2026 1st Quarter Material for Investor Conference (both via the company's IR library feed)
signals.implies: Glory's cash-automation arm is growing a third faster in EMEA than anywhere else, and its operating profit overseas has doubled — so expect harder direct engagement and more aggressive pricing on the recycler line Printec resells (Glory/Sesami TCRs, Printec cash-automation line). The practical risk is disintermediation: as EMEA becomes Glory's biggest region, Glory Global Solutions has more reason to sell direct or to re-cut distribution in CEE. Printec should lock its Glory-based accounts (Bank of Cyprus TCRs, and the wider branch cash-automation base) into multi-year managed-service wrappers that Glory cannot easily replicate, and use the Acrelec growth line as a warning that Glory now also competes with Printec's self-service and bank-kiosk business, not just its cash machines.

signals.entity: Glory Ltd — ECB euro banknote redesign as a demand driver
signals.country: Austria, Croatia, Cyprus, Greece, Slovakia, Slovenia (euro-area footprint)
signals.signal: In its 07/08/2026 investor conference material Glory devotes a slide to the 'ECB Euro Project' and tells investors that on 23/07/2026 the ECB released 10 candidate designs for the new euro banknote series and opened a public vote. Glory's stated read: cash usage 'is expected to remain firmly established in Europe', cash-infrastructure updates will therefore continue, and 'special demand related to banknote redesign is expected from around 2029' — issued in stages, so the demand may run for several years. This is a vendor putting a dated, multi-year hardware-refresh cycle into its own investor guidance. In plain terms: when a banknote series is redesigned, every machine that authenticates or sorts notes — teller cash recyclers (TCRs, the counter machines that both take in and pay out cash), banknote sorters, ATM deposit and recycling modules, retail cash recyclers — needs new recognition sensors, new note templates or outright replacement, and every one of them must be re-certified.
signals.source_name: GLORY LTD. — FY2026 1st Quarter Material for Investor Conference, slide 'Overseas Market Topics — ECB Euro Project'
signals.implies: This is the single largest forward driver for Printec's cash-automation line (Glory/Sesami TCRs, NCR recycling ATMs, banknote counting and sorting) across the six euro-area footprint countries, and it also lands on the NCR intelligent-deposit and recycling ATM estate Printec maintains. Because it hits recognition software and sensors rather than whole machines, it is mostly a SERVICE and UPGRADE annuity — exactly where Printec's field organisation is strong and where a pure OEM is weak. Printec should start the conversation now with the euro-area central banks and the large branch networks (Alpha Bank, BCR-adjacent euro entities, Erste Croatia, Bank of Cyprus) about a phased recognition-upgrade and re-certification programme, so the budget lines are shaped before 2029 rather than tendered as a single OEM package.
signals.likelihood: ECB design vote concludes and the series is confirmed within 12 months; procurement shaping starts 2027-2028, deliveries from ~2029
signals.followup: Track the ECB design-vote outcome and the ECB's published issuance timetable; open an upgrade-programme dialogue with Bank of Greece, Central Bank of Cyprus, Banka Slovenije, Národná banka Slovenska, HNB and OeNB, and with the euro-area commercial branch networks, during 2027 budget planning.
